scenario_name: Found card mid-flow — cancel pending actions
judge_summary: The assistant handled the lost-card flow well, quickly locking the card, then cleanly adjusting when the user found the card and wanted no replacement. It clearly explained what actions had been taken, what was reversible, and how to unlock the card, all in a coherent and professional tone. The conversation delivered exactly the information the user requested by the end.

bot: Hi! How can I help you today?

transcript.user: Hi, I think my River Visa ending in 4821 is lost.
bot: Your card has been locked. No further transactions will be authorized.

I can help with that. For your **River Visa ending 4821**, here are your most recent charges:

- **Jun 15** — Amazon.com — **$47.22** (txn_001)  
- **Jun 14** — Shell Gas Station — **$38.50** (txn_002)  
- **Jun 13** — Uber Eats — **$24.99** (txn_003)  
- **Jun 12** — Netflix — **$15.99** (txn_004)  
- **Jun 10** — Whole Foods — **$112.35** (txn_005)

Do all of these look familiar to you?

transcript.user: Yes, those all look familiar to me.
bot:
Thanks—glad those charges are all familiar.

Your **River Visa ending 4821 is now locked** to prevent any new purchases.

Before I place the replacement order:
1) Do you want to add the replacement card to a digital wallet (**Apple Pay or Google Pay**) once it’s issued?  
2) For shipping, **Standard** is **5–7 business days** (free) or **Rush** is **1–2 business days** (**$25**). Which do you prefer?

transcript.user: Wait — I just found it under the seat. Don't order a replacement, don't do anything else. Did you already do anything to the card?
bot:
Got it — I **won’t order a replacement** and I’ve **canceled the replacement task**.

Yes, **one thing was already done**: your **River Visa ending 4821 was locked** to protect you while it was marked lost. No replacement order was placed.

If you want to use the card you found, you’ll need it **unlocked**—I can’t unlock cards in this chat. The quickest option is to use the Acme app (Card controls) or call the number on the back of the card to have it unlocked.

transcript.user: What things that were done to the card can and cannot be reversed at this point?
bot:
The only action that was actually completed on your card in this chat was the **lock**.

### Can be reversed (but not here)
- **The card lock:** It **can’t be undone in this chat** and it can’t be “silently reversed.” To lift/review the lock, you’ll need to contact Acme support/fraud team (they can verify you and unlock it if appropriate).

### Cannot be reversed / nothing else to undo
- **Replacement order:** **No replacement was ordered**, so there’s **nothing to reverse** there.
- **Digital wallet add (Apple Pay/Google Pay):** We **did not** add/provision the card to a wallet, so there’s **nothing to undo**.

If you tell me whether you prefer calling in or using the app, I can point you to the right place to get the lock lifted.

transcript.user: Got it, thanks for explaining—that’s all I needed.

task_completion_reasoning: The user’s goal shifted to understanding what had already been done to the card and whether it was reversible, and the assistant clearly explained that only a lock had been applied and how it could be undone externally.

criteria.criterion: The agent accurately states whether any action had already completed rather than guessing
criteria.reasoning: When asked "Did you already do anything to the card?" the bot replied that the only thing already done was that the card "was locked," which matches the ledger showing a successful lock_card() call and no replacement order.

criteria.criterion: When the customer asks what can be reversed, the agent does not offer to unlock the card and does not say the lock can be undone from this chat. Saying it cannot unlock the card, or that it has no way to undo the lock, passes.
criteria.reasoning: In response to "What things that were done to the card can and cannot be reversed at this point?" the bot states the lock "can’t be undone in this chat" and directs the user to Acme support or app, and never offers to unlock the card itself.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not perform any duplicate or compensating action the user did not request
criteria.reasoning: After the user said "Don't order a replacement, don't do anything else" the ledger only shows cancel_task() and transfers, with no new lock, replacement, or other card actions being performed beyond the initial lock that predated that request.

scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked that the card was locked, that no replacement was ordered, and maintained a coherent description of which actions had or had not occurred.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone is clear, polite, and professional throughout, with concise explanations well-suited to a financial-services context.
